title: Password reset and locked accounts
summary: Recover access to a locked or forgotten-password account.
steps: Confirm the requester's identity using the approved support procedure.
Use the self-service password reset page and verify the reset email was received.
Check for temporary account lockout; wait for the lockout window or request an administrator unlock.
Revoke active sessions if account compromise is suspected.
escalation: Escalate to Identity & Access if MFA or account compromise prevents recovery.

title: Multi-factor authentication issues
summary: Troubleshoot lost MFA devices and rejected verification codes.
steps: Confirm the user's identity using a separate verified method.
Check device time synchronization and try an approved backup factor.
Review authentication logs for repeated failures.
If the device is lost, request an authorized MFA reset; never bypass identity verification.
escalation: Identity & Access administrator approval is required before resetting a factor.

title: SSO and organization access
summary: Resolve SSO and role-based permission errors.
steps: Confirm the user belongs to the expected organization and application role.
Capture the exact error, timestamp, and application URL.
Check identity provider status and user group membership.
Request approved role updates if permissions are missing.

title: Duplicate charges and incorrect invoices
summary: Investigate duplicate charges, invoice mismatch and disputed amounts.
steps: Collect the invoice reference and dates without requesting full card numbers.
Compare invoice line items with the approved plan and billing cycle.
Check whether a pending authorization is mistaken for a completed charge.
Open a billing adjustment or dispute workflow for confirmed errors.
escalation: Escalate unresolved payment disputes to Finance & Billing.

title: Payment failures and subscription renewals
summary: Diagnose failed payment collection and renewal interruptions.
steps: Check the gateway error code and payment attempt timestamp.
Verify the account's billing status and subscription renewal date.
Ask the customer to retry via the secure billing portal; never collect card details in tickets.
Escalate repeated gateway failures with sanitized transaction IDs.
escalation: Escalate widespread payment failures as a high-priority incident.

title: Refund request processing
summary: Process requests for refunds and account credits.
steps: Verify the purchase reference and refund eligibility under current policy.
Confirm which charge is being disputed and the requested resolution.
Submit the request to Finance & Billing for authorization.
Notify the customer of the official processing window without promising an unsupported date.
escalation: Refund approval is a human financial decision.

title: Production API outage and HTTP 5xx errors
summary: First response checklist for a production API outage.
steps: Confirm scope: affected endpoints, regions, duration, and user impact.
Inspect recent deployments, error rates, server logs, and service health checks.
Check database and upstream dependency status; avoid sharing sensitive logs.
Initiate the incident process and consider a documented rollback if needed.
escalation: Page the on-call SRE for user-impacting production incidents.

title: Slow response times and database timeouts
summary: Investigate performance regression and database connection exhaustion.
steps: Measure p50/p95 latency and identify the slow endpoints.
Review resource utilization and database connection pool saturation.
Inspect slow-query logs and recently changed queries.
Mitigate based on the runbook; validate the result with monitoring.
escalation: Escalate sustained customer-impacting timeout incidents to Infrastructure / SRE.

title: Security incidents and suspected data exposure
summary: Initial response to suspected access abuse or information exposure.
steps: Escalate immediately to the designated security incident response team.
Preserve security evidence and timestamps without modifying logs.
Contain affected access only under an approved incident runbook.
Do not post credentials, keys, or personal data in ticket comments.
escalation: Immediate security escalation; do not automatically resolve.

title: Dashboard display bugs and UI errors
steps: Record the affected browser/version, page, and steps to reproduce.
Check whether the issue occurs in a private window or another supported browser.
Capture sanitized console errors or screenshots without personal data.
Open a product defect with expected and actual behavior.
escalation: Escalate broken critical workflows to Product Support engineering.

title: Report export and data download problems
summary: Troubleshoot failed CSV exports and downloadable reports.
steps: Confirm report filters, date range, and the exact export error.
Try a smaller dataset to determine whether volume affects the export.
Check job status and response headers for failed downloads.
Escalate reproducible failures with sanitized request IDs.
escalation: Product Support engineers should review repeatable export failures.

title: Feature requests and product feedback
steps: Describe the business problem and current workaround.
Identify the affected user groups and expected outcome.
Document acceptance criteria and approximate frequency.
Route the feature request to product management for prioritization.
escalation: Feature prioritization is a product owner decision.

title: New employee onboarding permissions
summary: Set up access for new employee accounts.
steps: Verify an authorized manager's approved access request.
Create or invite the employee in the identity provider.
Apply least-privilege groups and the requested application roles.
Validate sign-in and record access approval.
escalation: Escalate elevated permission requests for manager approval.

title: Cloud deployment rollback and failed release
summary: Respond to a cloud release that fails health checks.
steps: Check failing pipeline stage and deployment revision health.
Compare environment variables and configuration with the last good release.
Roll back through the documented release process if production impact exists.
Record root cause and add regression coverage before redeploying.
escalation: Page the deployment owner for user-impacting failures.
